authoring.value:
The triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy
$$

is defined over the type I region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,-2\le y\le 4,\,0\le z\le 1+xy}.
$$

Use $[a,b]$ as the full nonempty projection of the exactly specified region $R$ onto the $y$ axis. The inner limits may be piecewise. What is $a+b?$

authoring.question: q-161495
authoring.value:
The inequalities defining $R$ are retained exactly. For every $y\in[-2,4]$, choosing $x=0$ leaves the nonempty fiber $0\le z\le1$. Thus the full nonempty $y$ projection is $[a,b]=[-2,4]$ and $a+b=2$.

The base must also satisfy $1+xy\ge0$. When $y<0$, this requires $x\le-1/y$. The bounds $y^2$ and $-1/y$ meet at $y=-1$. Hence

$$\iiint_R f\,dV=\int_{-2}^{-1}\int_0^{-1/y}\int_0^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy+\int_{-1}^4\int_0^{y^2}\int_0^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy.$$

On the first branch the $x$ cap is $-1/y$; on the second it is $y^2$. The source solution used $x\le y^2$ throughout and therefore included reversed $z$ bounds for some negative $y$. Its isolated expression $1+xz$ is also a transcription error: the upper $z$ bound is $1+xy$. These solution errors do not change the correct endpoint sum $2$.
